content:
sara nguyen: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm worried our continuous-batcher's queue shape (flat vs splay) is causing tail-latency spikes for small requests. Anyone seen similar in prod traces?

timothy cole: yup, noticed p99 jumps last night around 02:15. short requests did better on average but long-tail got worse. suspect coalesce window + head-of-line blocking.

lee park: flat queues = simple fairness, good for predictable throughput. splay/tiered queues pack similar seq-lens which improves avg cost, but you can get HOL blocking if a big seq sits in front.

anika singh: what about deadline hints + soft-priority? sketched variant: small-request fastpath queue + main coalesce queue that can preempt when deadline expires.

sara nguyen: here's a small config I tried in staging to reproduce the pattern:
```
batcher:
  queues:
    - name: fastpath
      max_tokens: 64
      preemptible: true
    - name: main
      max_tokens: 1024
      coalesce_window_ms: 8
  eviction_policy: deadline_hint
```

timothy cole: looks reasonable. two things to watch: starvation of main when fastpath is noisy, and metric coverage. need per-queue wait_p50/p95/p99, enqueue_reject, preempt_count.

lee park: we tried an admission-credit ledger in branch `lease-ledger-2`. it reduces starvation by allocating per-tenant credits and letting queues borrow up to a cap. prevents fastpath from hogging.

anika singh: can we validate with traffic replay? I'll run a 1h mixed workload replay (short:40%, medium:40%, long:20%) against both configs and capture tail-latency + KV-cache hit deltas.

sara nguyen: also worried about KV-cache affinity when we preempt/flush — might increase mem churn and hurt long requests. worth measuring cache reuse across preempt boundaries.

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed `batcher-v2` to us-west with 20% traffic (ids: canary/49888).

timothy cole: quick canary notes: p50 for <64 token requests down ~10ms, but p99 up ~30ms in spikes correlated with big seqs joining the main queue. also saw a handful of enqueue_rejects when credits dipped.

sara nguyen: :thinking_face: that's the tradeoff — better avg but worse tail. proposal: soft-isolation + lazy preempt: only force-preempt if wait_time > threshold AND estimated saved tokens > cost_of_preempt.

lee park: add leases to that: when we preempt, give the requester a short lease (50ms) so repeated preempts don't oscillate. simple backoff on subsequent preempt attempts.

anika singh: sounds good. I'll add the lease ledger to the replay and include a KV-cache reuse metric (per-tenant cache-hit-over-time). plan: run replay + canary correlation and produce a short results doc.

sara nguyen: action items: @anika run replay and publish results, @tim monitor canary metrics and flag regressions, @lee prototype lease ledger + backoff. I'll draft follow-up RFC with simulation numbers and preferred config.

timothy cole: sgtm. also recommend adding a telemetry tag for "preempt_reason" so we can attribute tail spikes precisely.

lee park: i'll push a small prototype today to `lease-ledger-exp` and add tests for starvation scenarios.

anika singh: will create a benchmark ticket and link runs.

sara nguyen: thanks team. follow-up meeting tomorrow if results show >20% p99 regression. :+1:
